title: Grandvalira & Pal-Arinsal: Andorra's Six-Sector Week

bestPeriod.window: Mid-January-mid-March, with the second half of January the sweet spot for snow depth against crowds
bestPeriod.avoid: 26 December-6 January (Spanish and French holidays collide, Pas de la Casa queues double) and after 10 April, when south-facing Encamp and El Tarter go to slush by 11:00
bestPeriod.raw: Mid-January-mid-March, with the second half of January the sweet spot for snow depth against crowds

accommodation.note: Soldeu/El Tarter 3-4 half board €90, €150 pppn; Andorra la Vella cuts this by a third

food.note: Mountain restaurant mains €14, €22; valley menú del dia €16, €20; Andorran alcohol duty is low

transport.note: Toulouse or Barcelona shared transfer €55, €90 each way; local L4/L2 bus €2, €5 per hop

activities.note: 6-day area pass roughly €300, €360, Caldea 3 h ~€45, one day of ski school or hire extras

profile.difficultyNote: 3/5, six lift-served days with 4,000-7,000 vertical metres of descent, no touring required, but two long circuits demand a full day on your feet at 2,000-2,600 m

gatewayAirport: TLS Toulouse-Blagnac, 3 h-3 h 30 by road to Soldeu; BCN Barcelona El Prat, 3 h-3 h 45; LEU Andorra-La Seu d'Urgell, 45 min but almost no scheduled traffic
summary: Andorra sells itself on volume, and for once the claim survives contact: Grandvalira alone strings six sectors across two valleys and a border ridge, and the joint Grandvalira Resorts ticket bolts on Pal-Arinsal and Ordino-Arcalís on the far side of the country. The week is built as a west-to-east sweep, start soft on Encamp and Canillo, spend the middle days working the Soldeu-Grau Roig spine and the Avet World Cup pitch, cross to Pas de la Casa for the French-facing snow, then break out to Arcalís for the one genuinely serious freeride mountain in the principality. It suits confident intermediates and better, families who want a lot of blue mileage without repetition, and anyone who likes the idea of finishing a ski day in a duty-free thermal spa. What it does not suit is the skier chasing Alpine altitude: the top here is 2,640 m and the bottom stations sit at 1,550-1,710 m, so snowmaking, not elevation, is what holds the week together.

itinerary.title: Land, transfer, and open the legs on Canillo
itinerary.morning: Fly into Toulouse or Barcelona and take a pre-booked shared transfer up the CG2. From Barcelona the road climbs through La Seu d'Urgell and the Andorran customs post at Sant Julià de Lòria; from Toulouse you come over the Pas de la Casa side and drop past Grau Roig, which is the better first view.
itinerary.afternoon: Collect hire gear at Viladomat in El Tarter, then ride the Canillo gondola from 1,550 m and ski the wide, quiet blues off Tossal de la Llosada. Canillo is the least-skied sector and the right place to find your feet.
itinerary.evening: Sol i Neu in Soldeu, the village's long-running restaurant-bar on the main road, for grilled meats and a first look at the après crowd next door.
itinerary.dayStats: Transfer 3 h-3 h 45 / Canillo gondola 1,550 m base / 2-3 h skiing, roughly 1,200 m vertical / hire €90, €140 for the week

itinerary.title: Soldeu, Espiolets and a first look at the Avet
itinerary.morning: Up the Soldeu gondola to Espiolets at 2,250 m, the biggest beginner plateau in the country and also the hub for everything above it. Warm up on Esparver and Àliga, then take the Solanelles chair for the long reds toward Riba Escorjada.
itinerary.afternoon: Inspect the **Avet**, Soldeu's FIS-homologated World Cup black that drops back into the village. The top pitch is steeper and narrower than its reputation; ski it once early, then again after 15:00 when the surface has been scraped clean and honest.
itinerary.evening: L'Abarset at the Soldeu base for the ski-boot après hour, then dinner at Ibaya in the Sport Hotel Hermitage if you want the fine-dining end of the valley.
itinerary.dayStats: 25-30 piste km / roughly 4,500 m descent / Espiolets 2,250 m / Avet vertical about 500 m to the village

itinerary.title: The Funicamp run: Encamp to Grau Roig and the Pessons cirque
itinerary.morning: Take the L4 bus down to Encamp at 1,300 m and ride the **Funicamp**, roughly 6 km of gondola to Cortals d'Encamp. It is a 20-plus-minute ride; do it before 10:00 or queue behind the day-trippers from Andorra la Vella.
itinerary.afternoon: Work west into **Grau Roig** and lap the **Pessons cirque**, a natural amphitheatre of chairs at 2,300-2,600 m with the best-preserved snow in Grandvalira. Lunch at the Refugi dels Llacs de Pessons. Then decide: return over the ridge to Soldeu, or drop back down the Funicamp.
itinerary.evening: Bus into Andorra la Vella and eat at Borda Estevet, a converted stone farm building on the Carretera de la Comella, escudella, grilled lamb and a Costers del Segre red.
itinerary.dayStats: Funicamp roughly 6,000 m of cable, 1,300 m to over 2,500 m / Pessons cirque 2,300-2,600 m / 30+ piste km / last ridge crossing to Soldeu by 15:30

itinerary.title: Pas de la Casa, the French frontier and duty-free
itinerary.morning: Ski the full eastern traverse from Soldeu through Grau Roig and over the Coll Blanc ridge into **Pas de la Casa**. This is the north- and east-facing corner of the resort at 2,050-2,640 m and it holds cold snow when everything else is turning.
itinerary.afternoon: Lap Pic Blanc and the Font Negre bowl, then ski down into Pas de la Casa town itself, which is less a village than a duty-free retail park at 2,050 m. Buy alcohol, tobacco, perfume or electronics here at Andorran rates, but know the allowances before you cross a border with them.
itinerary.evening: Return over the ridge no later than 15:00, or accept the L4 bus home. Dinner at El Rusc or Borda Xixerella over in the Erts/La Massana side if you have a car; otherwise Slalom in Soldeu.
itinerary.dayStats: Pas de la Casa 2,050-2,640 m / traverse Soldeu-Pas roughly 15 km each way / hard turnaround 15:00 / L4 bus fallback €2, €5

itinerary.title: Weather-contingency and rest day: Caldea, Canillo and the valley
itinerary.morning: This is the designed flex day. If the forecast is a whiteout or a foehn wind has shut the high chairs, take it now; if the week has been kind, take it anyway on day five when legs are worst. Start at the **Palau de Gel** in Canillo, Olympic rink, pool, and a warm building.
itinerary.afternoon: Bus to Escaldes-Engordany for **Caldea**, the glass tower fed by 70°C sulphur springs, or its adults-only sibling **Inúu**. Three hours is the standard ticket, roughly €45; the outdoor lagoon in falling snow is the reason people come.
itinerary.evening: Can Manel on Carrer Mestre Xavier Plana in Andorra la Vella for Catalan-Andorran cooking, then walk the Meritxell shopping strip. Andorra has no VAT in the EU sense, a 4.5% IGI instead, which is why the strip exists.
itinerary.dayStats: Caldea 3 h ~€45, Inúu supplement / Palau de Gel entry €10, €18 / zero vertical metres, which is the point / snowshoe alternative at Grau Roig, 2-3 h circuits

itinerary.title: Cross the country: Ordino-Arcalís and the freeride day
itinerary.morning: Drive or bus west across Andorra to **Ordino-Arcalís**, the far northern valley, 1,940-2,625 m, high, north-facing and the only sector here that feels like a proper mountain rather than a lift network. Your multi-day Grandvalira pass already covers it.
itinerary.afternoon: Ride the Creussans chair and work the terrain toward **Port de Rat** and under **Pic de Casamanya**. If there is fresh snow, book a guide through Andorra Guies rather than pointing at a line yourself; carry transceiver, shovel and probe and check meteo.ad before you leave the hotel.
itinerary.evening: Eat in Ordino village at Restaurant Armengol or the Quo Vadis, then drive back over the Coll d'Ordino. Allow 45-60 minutes.
itinerary.dayStats: Ordino-Arcalís 1,940-2,625 m, roughly 30 km pisted / drive from El Tarter 50-70 min / avalanche bulletin meteo.ad, EAWS 1-5 / guide €280, €400 per day for a group

itinerary.title: Pal-Arinsal, then out
itinerary.morning: Last ski day at **Pal-Arinsal**, the third resort on your pass, 1,550-2,560 m, about 63 km, tree-lined at Pal and open above Arinsal, and the friendliest sector for a relaxed final morning. The Vallnord-era gondolas from La Massana and Arinsal put you on snow fast with luggage left at the hotel.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski until 13:00, return hire gear, then transfer. From La Massana the run to Barcelona is 3 h-3 h 45; to Toulouse 3 h-3 h 30 including the customs stop, which is a real stop with real queues on Sunday afternoons.
itinerary.evening: If your flight is early, sleep at the border in La Seu d'Urgell or at an airport hotel rather than chancing the CG1 in snow.
itinerary.dayStats: Pal-Arinsal 1,550-2,560 m, roughly 63 km / half-day 2,500-3,000 m descent / customs queue allowance 30-60 min on Sundays / airport transfer 3 h+

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Nordic
accommodationStrategy.description: On the road at El Tarter within a short walk or shuttle hop of the gondola, with ski room, pool and half board that matters when the nearest supermarket is a bus ride away. Central on the valley axis: Canillo, Soldeu and the Funicamp at Encamp are all inside 20 minutes on the L4. Roughly €90, €140 pppn half board in high season.

accommodationStrategy.name: Sport Hotel Hermitage & Spa
accommodationStrategy.description: The luxury anchor at the foot of the Soldeu gondola, with the Sport Wellness Mountain Spa and two serious restaurants, Ibaya and the Japanese Koy Hermitage. Ski to the door and pay for it: €300, €500 per room. Book it if comfort, not mileage, is the point.

accommodationStrategy.name: Andorra Park Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: The counter-strategy: sleep in the capital, save 30-40% on the bed, walk to Caldea and the shops, and commute to snow via the Funicamp at Encamp ten minutes away, which lands you high. The cost is 25-40 minutes each way and no ski-in/ski-out. Roughly €130, €220 per room.

logistics.connectivity: Andorra Telecom (Mobiland) is the sole operator and Andorra sits **outside EU roaming**, EU and UK bundles do not apply and charges are steep. Kill data roaming at the border, use lift-station wifi, and download offline maps and the Grandvalira app first.
logistics.emergency: 112 reaches the Bombers d'Andorra, who run mountain rescue. Andorra is **not in the EU**, so EHIC/GHIC does not apply, carry insurance naming winter sports, off-piste and helicopter recovery. The hospital is Nostra Senyora de Meritxell, Escaldes-Engordany.
logistics.weather: The **foehn** can lift freezing levels 1,000 m in hours and shut top chairs on wind; Mediterranean lows dump heavy wet snow on the eastern sectors and close the **Port d'Envalira** at 2,408 m, Europe's highest paved pass and the road to France. Check the CG2 before any Pas de la Casa plan.
logistics.bookingWindows: Season passes cheapest in the Early Booking window closing 30 June; day and multi-day passes are dynamic and cheapest 7-14 days ahead online. February half-term beds in Soldeu and El Tarter go 3-4 months out. Caldea weekend slots 2-3 days ahead. Freeride guides are unbookable on a powder morning, reserve on spec.
logistics.money: Andorra uses the **euro** by monetary agreement but is outside the EU and has no VAT, a 4.5% IGI instead. Cards are universal; small refuges prefer cash. Tipping is rounding up.
logistics.transportRules: Winter tyres or chains are legally required in winter conditions and enforced. **Customs checks apply entering and leaving at both the Spanish and French borders**, carry passports and know your duty-free allowance. Multi-day passes upgrade automatically to the three-resort ticket; the Mobile Pass runs on Bluetooth, so keep the phone charged and out of a metal-lined pocket.
logistics.permits: No park fees. Drones require Andorran authorisation and are banned over the ski areas. Off-piste is legal, but ducking closure ropes voids resort liability and, in practice, your insurance.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable. Altitude is modest at 2,640 m top, but Pas de la Casa at 2,050 m plus alcohol plus dehydration produces the classic day-two headache. The avalanche bulletin is **meteo.ad**, read it yourself, not the hotel's summary.

proTips: Never buy two consecutive single-day passes. Any Grandvalira pass of two or more days automatically becomes the Grandvalira Resorts area pass and hands you Pal-Arinsal and Ordino-Arcalís for nothing.
Sleep at El Tarter or Canillo rather than Soldeu, same lift network, 15-25% cheaper beds, and a fraction of the 09:00 gondola queue.
Ride the Funicamp from Encamp on the busiest day of the week. Everyone else drives to Soldeu; Encamp's 1,300 m base puts you at 2,500 m in one ride and bypasses the crush entirely.
Ski the Avet twice in a day, 10:00 on the overnight groom, and after 15:00 once it has been scraped to the boilerplate the racers actually deal with. It is a different run.
Book Caldea for a weekday afternoon, and book Inúu instead if you are over 16: identical thermal source, a fraction of the population.
Turn off data roaming at the customs post. Andorra sits outside the EU roaming zone and this is the single most common bill shock of the trip.
Treat 15:00 as the latest you leave Pas de la Casa for Grau Roig. Missing it costs a €45, €60 taxi or a slow L4 bus in ski boots.
If fresh snow lands, abandon the plan and go to Ordino-Arcalís that morning, not two days later. It is the only place in Andorra where powder survives a full day of traffic.

raw.Pass tiers by name: The **Grandvalira pass** covers the six eastern sectors, indicatively **€60, €72 adult/day**, **€330, €390 for 6 days adult**, **€215, €260 child (6-11)**, all dynamic. Critically, any pass of **two or more consecutive days upgrades automatically to the Grandvalira Resorts area pass**, adding Pal-Arinsal and Ordino-Arcalís free. The regional super-pass is the **Andorra Pass** season ticket across all three, published for 2026/27 at **€885 non-resident in Early Booking to 30 June, €1,019 from 1 July**; the northern-valleys **Nord Pass** at €668 rising to €788. Buy online for up to ~15% off gate price and use the **Mobile Pass**, 244 Bluetooth gates went in for 2025/26, replacing the keycard and its deposit. Night skiing is not a Grandvalira product; budget no floodlit supplement.
raw.Lift network and circuits: The spine runs Encamp → Grau Roig → Pas de la Casa one way, Encamp → Canillo → El Tarter → Soldeu → Grau Roig the other. The **Funicamp gondola** from Encamp at 1,300 m is the key piece, roughly 6 km of cable to Cortals d'Encamp above 2,500 m, one of Europe's longest, letting you sleep in the valley and reach Grau Roig in 25 minutes. Coll Blanc and the Pessons bowls carry you over the 2,500 m ridge to Pas de la Casa; the **Canillo-El Forn gondola** lifts 1,550 m into Canillo, which links east over Tossal de la Llosada and Espiolets. The **Encamp-to-Pas-and-back-to-Canillo circuit is a full day**: 40-45 piste km, eight to ten lifts.
raw.Last lift home: Lifts run roughly 09:00-16:30. The two links that strand people are Pas de la Casa back to Grau Roig, and the Espiolets/Tossal chain from Soldeu to Canillo, treat **15:00 as the hard turnaround at Pas de la Casa, 15:30 at Soldeu**. The patch is the road: the **L4 bus** works the CG2 between Encamp, Canillo, El Tarter, Soldeu and Pas de la Casa for €2, €5; a taxi Pas-Soldeu is €45, €60.
raw.Snow reliability: Grandvalira spans **1,710-2,640 m**, Pal-Arinsal 1,550-2,560 m, Ordino-Arcalís 1,940-2,625 m. Pas de la Casa and Grau Roig face north and east onto the French frontier and hold natural snow; Encamp, Canillo and El Tarter are lower, sunnier, snowmaking-dependent. Roughly **€11 m went into snow production for 2025/26**, 53 new guns plus 118 replacements at about 90% less energy, a 100,000 m³ reservoir at Lake Vaquer, 36,000 m³ at Ordino-Arcalís, 3 km of new Soldeu-El Tarter pipe. Coverage is high, plausibly ~70% of pisted km, but unpublished, treat as unverified. **Season: late November to mid-April.** In a bad year the resort retreats to the Grau Roig-Pas de la Casa bowls and the Espiolets plateau, closes the valley returns and sends you down by gondola.
raw.Off-piste and touring: The freeride mountain is **Ordino-Arcalís**, terrain skier's left of the Creussans chair and the bowls under **Pic de Casamanya** and **Port de Rat**, with a lift-accessed freeride zone and transceiver checkpoint. In Grandvalira the **Pessons cirque** gives long mellow off-piste, and the old **TK Bosc** drag at Soldeu was removed for 2025/26 to open a tree-freeride sector. Bulletin: **Servei Meteorològic Nacional d'Andorra** (meteo.ad), EAWS 1-5. No legal guide requirement, but this is a persistent-weak-layer snowpack with slow rescue: use **Andorra Guies** or a Grandvalira freeride guide, €280, €400 per day per group.
raw.Piste breakdown: Grandvalira publishes about **210 km over 130 runs**; Pal-Arinsal adds ~63 km, Ordino-Arcalís ~30 km, around **300 km** on the joint ticket, roughly 20% green, 30% blue, 35% red, 15% black. **Beginners** belong at Encamp's Cortals plateau, El Tarter's Riba Escorjada and lower Pal. **Intermediates** own the Soldeu-Grau Roig axis, lapping Solanelles and Coll Blanc. **Experts** get three things: the **Avet** black at Soldeu (the FIS World Cup piste of the 2019 Finals, steeper and narrower up top than its reputation), the Pic Blanc blacks at Pas de la Casa, and Arcalís.
raw.Non-ski days: **Caldea and Inúu** at Escaldes-Engordany, southern Europe's largest thermal complex on 70°C sulphur springs, three hours around €45, Inúu the adults-only annexe. **Palau de Gel** in Canillo has an Olympic rink and pool. Marked **snowshoe circuits at Grau Roig and the Juclà lakes**, dog-sledding at Grau Roig, and the 5 km-plus **Tobotronc** alpine coaster at Naturlandia.
raw.Hire, lockers and schools: Every base has a Grandvalira rental; **Viladomat** (Soldeu, El Tarter, Canillo) is the reliable independent, **€90, €140 a week** standard, €160, €220 performance. Lockers at Espiolets and Grau Roig €5, €8 a day. The **Escola d'Esquí i Snowboard de Grandvalira** runs roughly **€150, €220 for five half-day group mornings**, **€60, €90 an hour** private.

sources.verified: Grandvalira Resorts' published €39 m investment for 2025/26 (€32.1 m Grandvalira, €2.9 m Pal Arinsal, €4 m Ordino Arcalís), including ~€11 m on snowmaking, 53 new plus 118 replacement guns, the 100,000 m³ Lake Vaquer and 36,000 m³ Ordino reservoirs, 3 km of new Soldeu-El Tarter pipe, the TK Eslàlom extension to 556 m / 229 m vertical, the new 70 m TK Refugi, the removal of TK Bosc at Soldeu for a freeride area, and 244 Bluetooth Mobile Pass gates. Grandvalira's own statement that passes of two or more consecutive days include Ordino-Arcalís and Pal-Arinsal, and that pricing is dynamic with ~15% savings for advance online purchase. Published 2026/27 Andorra Pass rates (€885 Early Booking / €1,019 from 1 July, non-resident) and Nord Pass (€668 / €788).
sources.confidenceNotes: **The 6-day adult and child prices quoted (€330, €390 and €215, €260) are an estimated band, not a confirmed tariff.** Grandvalira publishes no fixed multi-day price; the only firm reference found was a November 2024 sample of €378 adult / €240 child for six days. Re-verify against the live booking assistant for actual travel dates. Senior rates (~€43.50 for 65-69, ~€25 for 70-74, free at 75+) are also sample-date dependent. Keycard deposit amount unconfirmed and possibly obsolete under the Mobile Pass. **Snowmaking coverage as a percentage of pisted km is not published by Grandvalira**, the ~70% figure is inference and must be sourced or cut. Piste kilometres and the difficulty split are indicative. Funicamp length is widely quoted near 6 km but unconfirmed to the metre. Season dates, lift hours and last-crossing times shift year to year. Ski school, hire, Caldea and Palau de Gel prices are prior-season bands.
